Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Summary of key clinical findings, reasoning, and impressions: Patient (Jack Smith) presents with ~6 weeks of unilateral (left) hearing loss, intermittent left-sided tinnitus, and occasional mild imbalance/lightheadedness with some nausea. No ear pain, discharge, fever, chest pain, or palpitations reported. Examination has not yet occurred; clinician recommended in-person otoscopic examination to first exclude conductive causes (particularly cerumen impaction). Tinnitus education leaflet to be provided.  
- Relevant differentials from DDx that support/refine clinician impression: DDx supports high likelihood of cerumen impaction as initial cause and raises sensorineural causes (vestibular schwannoma, viral cochleitis/labyrinthitis, Meniere disease) as important considerations if otoscopy is normal.  
- Working diagnosis: Suspected cerumen (earwax) impaction causing conductive left-sided hearing loss (working diagnosis pending otoscopic examination). This is supported by unilateral muffled hearing without pain/discharge and explicit clinician suggestion in the transcript and by DDx ranking cerumen impaction as high likelihood.  
- Considerations (additional plausible but uncertain options from DDx): Vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma) — medium likelihood; viral cochleitis/labyrinthitis — medium likelihood; Meniere disease — low–medium likelihood. These remain considerations if otoscopy is normal or if symptoms progress; audiometry and possible imaging may be required.  
- Plan / actions taken: Arrange face-to-face clinic appointment within ~4–5 days for otoscopic ear exam (admin staff to schedule; patient advised to call support team number left in notes). Provide tinnitus information leaflet (link to be pasted in appointment notes). Safety-net and follow-up advice: return or rebook if symptoms worsen, new neurological signs, severe vertigo, or other acute concerns. No medications initiated during this encounter. If otoscopy is normal or sensorineural loss suspected, refer for formal audiometry and ENT review/imaging as indicated.  
- Conflict noted: Patient's statement regarding use of cotton buds is ambiguous in transcript; DDx notes ambiguity — use of cotton buds as risk factor for cerumen impaction is possible but not confirmed.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Cerumen (earwax) impaction / obstructive conductive hearing loss — High likelihood. Justification: Clinician explicitly suspected impacted wax; unilateral muffled hearing without pain/discharge or systemic signs is typical and symptoms can be masked by ambient sound.  
- Vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma) — Medium likelihood. Justification: Unilateral progressive hearing loss with unilateral tinnitus and mild imbalance fits vestibular nerve pathology; requires audiometry and imaging if otoscopy is normal.  
- Viral cochleitis / labyrinthitis — Medium likelihood. Justification: Inner-ear inflammation can cause unilateral hearing loss, tinnitus and dizziness; less likely without severe vertigo or fever but remains plausible if conductive causes excluded.
